quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyrie Irving on his perspective of the modern NBA
quotes.excerpt: I don't look at it as comparing my years to other people, but just how much love do I still have for it.
quotes.quote: I love those guys, but I don't share the same sentiments as in certain cases. I think I've been able to put the NBA in perspective, coming in at 19, 16 years. I don't look at it as comparing my years to other people, but just how much love do I still have for it. And it's not just for basketball. Basketball is an eternal flame, I'm always going to be around it. I love playing outside with my kids, with kids in the park. I love being in my backyard, lowering the rim, still dunking on people. Some of the little things that people kind of forget about, the small hoops in the house with my cousins, teaching the game, small hoop, playing with my son. So basketball is an eternal flame, but in terms of the NBA schedule and things of that nature, I think you got to really be in love with that too.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton on how NBA championship formulas have evolved
quotes.excerpt: Every three or four year window, every NBA year, it starts to become different on how people win championships.
quotes.quote: I always said that the game is like a every three or four year window. And every team is different on how every NBA year, it starts to become different on how people win championships. Like when I first got to the league, you needed two big men to win a championship. Then it went to you had to have a really good point guard and a big man. Then it went to you had to have a dynamic wing guy. Then it went to you had to have hybrid fours and being able to like have those hybrid fours be the point guard as a defacto, just like Draymond Green and win a championship. And now we're in a a wheel effect where you got to be able to put up a lot of threes in the game.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on how betting culture has changed NBA player focus
quotes.excerpt: We wouldn't even think about playing a parlay when we was hooping. We wouldn't even it didn't even cross our mind.
quotes.quote: It was like forbidden. We wouldn't even think about playing a parlay when we was hooping. We wouldn't even it didn't even cross our mind. You know what I'm saying? Like we was going to play cards on the plane, we was going to play in the hotel rooms, and that was going to be it. Like we weren't thinking about, you know, going to get a bookie and play with a parlay. We weren't thinking about none of that. But I think when you start adding all these betting apps and betting things, I mean, I'm not blaming Adam Silver because he's done nothing but amazing job at bringing more and more money to the table. But when you start seeing FanDuel, DraftKings, you start seeing all these different sponsors, I mean, some people, you can't blame Adam Silver for that.

quotes.summary_phrase: Charlie Villanueva on the extensive support staff for modern NBA teams

quotes.quote: Every team now has a has like a doctor that's the head of their you know, medical staff. Then they have trainers, they have like they have they have everybody. Like they have a whole staff around. Before, before we got to the league, before it changed, they was doing it for a month and still playing the full fucking season.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on the evolution of NBA training camp intensity
quotes.excerpt: We walked in the gym and training camp in Charlotte with Bernie Bickerstaff, we had stations.
quotes.quote: We walked in the gym and training camp in Charlotte with Bernie Bickerstaff, we had stations. Like like like weight room stations. Like we was like medicine balls, we was lifting weights, we was doing rows, we was doing all kind of stuff on the court. They had weight room stations in the in the in the gym.
